correctness.rationale: The additive-length classification is correct. For a nonzero target S=t+u with N(t)=N(u)=1, conjugation gives tu=S/bar(S), so t and u are the roots of X^2-SX+S/bar(S); after dividing the discriminant by S^2, the criterion is d=1-4/N(S). A repeated root gives d=0, while a distinct pair gives delta=(t-u)/S with bar(delta)=-delta, hence delta^2=d is a nonsquare in F_q. Conversely, d=0 or nonsquare explicitly produces norm-one roots S(1±delta)/2. Norm fibers have q+1 elements, so the two-sum count is (q^2+2q+3)/2. For every nonzero S outside T, beta↦N(S-beta) on T has fibers of size at most two and therefore image size at least (q+1)/2; this image must meet the (q+1)/2 admissible norm values inside the (q-1)-element group F_q^*, proving three-summability. Zero is a three-sum exactly when T meets T+T, i.e. when chi(-3) is 0 or -1. The stated length distribution then follows by norm-fiber counting. Fresh finite-field enumeration for q=3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23 reproduced the two- and three-fold sumsets and every L_j count.

originality.rationale: Shi-Li-Xia-Helleseth-Ozbudak's September 2026 preprint treats q=3^m and determines the corresponding norm-one-torus additive length in characteristic three. The audited theorem genuinely extends that exact unweighted problem to every odd prime power and exposes the new q≡1 (mod 3) endpoint where zero alone is missing from the exact three-fold sumset. The inspected 2023/2025 generalized Zetterberg covering-radius work treats related codes and coefficient structures, not this exact unweighted torus sumset and length distribution. Targeted searches found no earlier all-odd-q statement. The proof is short and the motivating preprint is very recent, so the priority claim remains appropriately qualified against folklore or near-simultaneous work.

scientific_value.rationale: The result closes the natural odd-characteristic extension posed by the recent decoding work with an exact, not merely bounded, additive diameter and complete length distribution. It also identifies precisely which characteristic-three simplification fails: T can be disjoint from T+T and exact three-fold coverage can miss zero. These formulas give a clean finite-field structural theorem even though they do not themselves yield maximum-likelihood decoders for every odd-characteristic code family.
